questions.question_text: What is the purpose of a 'Preflight Check'?
questions.correct_answer: To verify all aircraft systems are functioning properly before flight
questions.explanation: The preflight check is a systematic inspection of the aircraft to ensure all systems, controls, and equipment are in working order before takeoff.

questions.correct_answer: A systems check performed at the holding point before takeoff
questions.explanation: The Run-up Check is performed after preflight, at the designated holding point, to verify engine performance, flight controls, and instruments before requesting takeoff clearance.

questions.question_text: What does 'GUMPS' stand for in the landing checklist?
questions.explanation: GUMPS is a memory aid for final landing checks: Gear (down), Undercarriage, Mixture (rich/appropriate), Propeller (if variable pitch), and Switches (lights on).

questions.correct_answer: A turn exceeding 45 degrees of bank
questions.explanation: A steep turn is generally defined as any turn with a bank angle greater than 45 degrees. This maneuver is used to develop aircraft control skills.

questions.correct_answer: Adjusting flight controls to maintain desired flight attitude without constant pressure
questions.explanation: Trimming uses trim tabs or control surfaces to balance aerodynamic forces, allowing the pilot to maintain flight attitude without constant control pressure.
VFR (Visual Flight Rules) allows pilots to fly by reference to landmarks and weather visibility when conditions permit. It requires visual contact with the ground.
IFR (Instrument Flight Rules) governs flight when visibility is restricted. Pilots navigate using instruments and must file flight plans with air traffic control.

questions.correct_answer: Aborting a landing attempt and climbing back to altitude
questions.explanation: A Go-Around is executed when conditions aren't suitable for landing. The pilot adds power, climbs, and returns to the landing pattern for another approach.

questions.correct_answer: Angling the aircraft into the wind to maintain desired track
questions.explanation: Crosswind correction (crabbing) involves pointing the aircraft's nose into the wind at an angle to compensate and maintain the desired flight path over the ground.

questions.correct_answer: A maneuver where the aircraft moves sideways through the air while maintaining control
questions.explanation: A slip is an intentional maneuver where the aircraft is positioned at an angle to the relative wind, causing it to move sideways. It's useful for rapid descent or approach correction.
